title: Benchmark for Long-Context Safety: Harmful Instructions Buried in Long Documents
original_idea: Construct 100 scenarios placing a harmful instruction at varying positions within long benign documents (beginning, middle, end, buried in footnotes). Measure refusal rates as a function of instruction position and document length.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Long-context safety is poorly characterized and increasingly important as models handle longer inputs. Direct deployment relevance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generating long benign documents and embedding instructions requires some engineering. Running long-context inference needs more compute/time. Moderate difficulty.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 100 scenarios x multiple positions x multiple document lengths. Substantial content creation. Overlaps significantly with gen-0635 but at longer context and more positions.

novelty.reasoning: LongSafetyBench (2024) provides 10 task categories at an average length of 41,889 words, finding most mainstream LLMs have <50% safe responses in long-context scenarios. LongSafety (ACL 2025) offers 1,543 test cases across 7 safety issues and 6 task types. Both benchmarks establish that models overlook harmful content in long contexts and that position matters. The proposed 100-scenario benchmark with position variation (beginning, middle, end, footnotes) is a strict subset of these existing, published, and peer-reviewed benchmarks.

evidence: LongSafetyBench: Long-Context LLMs Struggle with Safety Issues. arXiv:2411.06899, 2024.
LongSafety: Evaluating Long-Context Safety of Large Language Models. ACL 2025, arXiv:2502.16971.
